previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with epistaxis and a supratherapeutic INR of 9.8, likely due to his warfarin therapy despite no recent medication or dietary changes. He had ongoing oozing and blood in his throat after initial management at an outside hospital with a nasal balloon catheter. He was given oral vitamin K and admitted for monitoring. ENT performed cauterization of a bleeding septal vessel with silver nitrate and Surgicell, achieving hemostasis. Warfarin was held during admission and restarted on discharge when his INR reached 2.8. Plavix was held for five days for safety and was to be resumed post-discharge. His baby aspirin was continued throughout due to his history of strokes. He remained stable, with no further bleeding, and was discharged home with visiting nurse INR monitoring and clear follow-up instructions.

of breath as well as increased lower leg edema. There was 
concern for possible fluid retention related to decreased heart 
function in the setting of possible increased intake of salt in 
your diet. You received an increased dose of lasix as well as 
nebulizers and your symptoms improved. An echocardiogram was 
performed which showed that your heart's ability to pump blood 
had slightly decreased compared to the previous echocardiogram 
of your heart. We have arranged for close outpatient follow-up 
with your primary care doctor and heart doctor for continued 
management of your heart issues.

- Please continue to take all of your other home medications as 
prescribed.

Please be sure to weigh yourself every morning; call your MD if 
your weight goes up more than 3 lbs.

Please be sure to have your visiting nurse check your INR when 
she sees you as she usually does. If your INR is not in the 
appropriate range then you will need to change your coumadin 
(warfarin) dose as directed.
.
Please be sure to keep all follow-up appointments with your PCP 
and heart doctor.
.
It was a pleasure taking care of you and we wish you a speedy 
recovery.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with history of chest pain and shortness of
breath.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired through the chest with and without IV
contrast.  Multiplanar reformations were obtained and reviewed.

CT OF THE CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST:

The thyroid gland is unremarkable.  There is no axillary or mediastinal
lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria.  The heart shows a replaced prosthetic
aortic valve, coronary artery calcifications, a left-sided pacer terminating
in the right atrium and ventricle appropriately.  No pericardial effusions are
present.  The aorta and great vessels are normal.  The pulmonary arteries are
patent down to the subsegmental level.  The airways are patent down to the
subsegmental level.  The lungs are normal with no effusions, consolidations,
or nodules seen.

Although this examination is not tailored for subdiaphragmatic evaluation. 
The liver, spleen, right kidney and partially imaged pancreas appear
unremarkable.  The left kidney has a simple upper pole cyst.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:

The visible osseous structures show minimal anterior osteophyte formation in
the thoracic spine.  Sternal wires are intact.  No suspicious lytic or blastic
lesions are present.

IMPRESSION:

No acute intrathoracic process.
